official.deadline_note: The University of Hawai'i at Manoa graduate application for the following fall semester is also due December 1; supporting documents for both the UH admissions office and department applications must be completed by January 10.
official.application_cycle: Annual international competition; current cycle opened August 2026 and closes December 1, 2026 for study beginning the following August
official.status_note: Application window is open (opened August 2026); applications close December 1, 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: "Full-time graduate tuition and fees ... for the academic year to the equivalent of the general tuition charged for post-baccalaureate students at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa toward master's or doctoral studies."
benefits: Full-time graduate tuition and fees up to the equivalent of the general tuition charged for post-baccalaureate students at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa
Housing in an East-West Center residence hall for the academic year, based on single occupancy
Funding for field study and conference presentations, offered on a competitive basis during the fellow's period of study
Automatic consideration for EWCA Alumni and Foundation scholarships, which may supplement the fellowship
eligibility: Citizens or permanent residents of the United States
Citizens of countries in the Pacific and Asia, including Russia (East-West Center publishes country lists for the Pacific Region, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia)
Minimum grade point average of 3.0 (4.0=A scale) or the equivalent in the last four semesters or six quarters of the undergraduate record and in all post-baccalaureate work
A 4-year bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited US college or university, or a recognized institution of higher learning abroad, obtained before the award starts
Admission to a University of Hawai'i at Manoa graduate program by December 1
requirements: Submit the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application during the annual competition

official.citizenship_residency: Citizens or permanent residents of the United States, or citizens of listed Pacific and Asian countries including Russia

official.description: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship provides master's and doctoral degree funding for graduate students from Asia, the Pacific and the United States to pursue study at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa while participating in the Center's residential, educational, cultural and leadership development programs in Honolulu.

applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship pays UH Manoa graduate tuition and fees plus single-occupancy dorm housing in Honolulu, with only partial help toward incidental expenses, so you must fund living costs yourself. The window is short and doubled: the East-West Center application and your UH Manoa graduate application are both due December 1, with all supporting documents wrapped up by January 10. Selection priority leans heavily on a demonstrated commitment to the Indo-Pacific region, so frame your statement around regional impact rather than academics alone.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates from Asia-Pacific countries, or US citizens and permanent residents, with a 3.0+ record pursuing a master's or PhD at UH Manoa in a field aligned with East-West Center priorities.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality appears on the East-West Center's published Pacific/Asia country lists before investing time
Start the UH Manoa graduate application in parallel - the university's online system opens August 1 and both applications are due December 1
Prepare transcripts with the GPA for your last four semesters or six quarters worked out to evidence the 3.0 minimum
Line up referees early; references are part of the fellowship application package
Plan to be in Honolulu from early-to-mid August for the mandatory Community Building Institute
common_rejection_risks: Missing the December 1 double deadline (both the East-West Center and UH Manoa applications)
A personal statement that does not evidence Indo-Pacific commitment, which the selection process prioritizes
Assuming the fellowship can support a family; East-West Center states it does not support spouses and dependents
Choosing a field of study with no connection to East-West Center goals
Leaving the supporting-document work past January 10 even when the UH department deadline is later
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the dorm room and partial incidental funding - food, personal expenses and any family costs; fellows living off-campus with family receive only an off-campus housing allowance equivalent to the single dorm rate from the second semester.
document_audit: Transcripts must evidence the 3.0 GPA over the last four semesters or six quarters; partial records slow review
Both the UH admissions office and department application files must be complete by January 10
Degree credentials from abroad must come from a recognized institution of higher learning
alerts: The fellowship cannot be deferred to another semester or year - reapply if you cannot start in residence
Living in East-West Center dormitories is required for fellows who are single or married with no dependents under 18
Renewal for the second year depends on funding availability and timely, satisfactory progress
Field study and conference funding is competitive and not guaranteed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the East-West Center fellowship application and the UH Manoa graduate application by December 1, complete both sets of supporting documents by January 10, and join the Community Building Institute in August.
